blocks.detail: Cut pile gives paws something to grip, nylon and triexta spring back from claws and daily thundering, and a firm pad keeps the nosing tight so the carpet does not slide. blocks.html: In the split-entry homes around Silver Lake and Eastmont, the dog goes up and down that one staircase thirty times a day. A common Reddit thread asks whether a big dog can safely use carpeted stairs at all. It can, as long as the carpet is picked for grip and recovery instead of softness. Here is the fiber, the pile, the pad and the install detail that make Everett stairs safe for a dog.

blocks.text: What a dog actually does to stair carpet

items.title: Claws twist on every tread
items.text: A dog does not step on a stair, it launches. Rear claws dig into the nosing and twist as it pushes off. Loops snag and unravel under that motion; cut pile just gets brushed, which is why it lasts longer.

items.title: Crushing in the same three inches
items.text: Dogs hit the same middle three inches of each tread every trip. Pile that cannot recover mats into a shiny track within a year. Nylon has the best crush recovery; polyester is soft on day one and flat by year two.

items.title: Wet paws and the occasional accident
items.text: Everett rain means damp paws on the stairs from October to May. Solution-dyed fiber, colored through the strand, shrugs off enzyme cleaners and bleach-based spot removers. Stock-dyed carpet loses color where you clean it most.

items.title: Hair and dander collection
items.text: Stairs are hard to vacuum, so hair packs into the corner where tread meets riser. Low, dense pile holds less of it and gives it up faster to a stair tool. Deep frieze on stairs is a hair trap.

blocks.text: Pad and installation details that keep a dog safe

items.html: Firm, dense pad, on the thinner side. A soft, thick pad lets the carpet roll over the nosing under a dog's weight, and that is how a paw slips. Stairs want a dense pad that keeps the tread edge crisp.
Waterfall over the nosing, not wrapped and tacked under. The carpet runs smoothly over the edge of each tread, so there is nothing for a claw to catch on and nothing to work loose.
No seams on a tread. A stair tread should be one piece of carpet. Seams on the nosing are the first thing a dog's claw finds and the first place the carpet fails.
Tack strip set back correctly. Everett split-entries often have a lower flight where the old strip sits too close to the riser. We reset it so the carpet stays tight with no ridge under the pad.

Stair treads need more fastening, not less. Each tread is stapled through the pad at the crotch of the step and stretched over the nosing. Loose stair carpet is dangerous for dog and owner alike, and ours carries a 1-year workmanship warranty.

blocks.text: When carpet on the stairs is the wrong call

items: Your dog is a heavy shedder and you will not vacuum the stairs weekly. Hair packed into the tread corners is the complaint we hear a year later.
The dog has a history of marking on the stairs. Carpet and pad both absorb urine, and no stain warranty covers the pad. Hardwood treads with a washable runner may serve you better.
You are selling within a year and the rest of the house is hardwood. Everett buyers coming from Seattle often expect bare wood stairs; see our note on replacing carpet before a sale.
The stairs are already hardwood and the dog slips. Try clear treads or a bound runner first; a full carpet install is more than the problem needs.
The staircase is open-sided with pie-shaped treads and you want a loop. A loop on a pie tread is a snag waiting to happen.

blocks.text: Checklist before you pick a stair carpet

items.html: Read the label for fiber and dye method. You want nylon or triexta, ideally solution-dyed. Ask the rep to point to those words, not to the marketing name.
Press the sample. Fold it backwards over your knuckle. If you see the backing easily, it is not dense enough for a stair nosing.
Test traction with your own dog. Our mobile showroom brings full samples to the house. Lay one on a tread and let the dog take a few steps.
Match color to the dog. A flecked mid tone near your dog's coat color hides hair between vacuuming. A black lab on cream carpet is a daily chore.
Get the tread count and pad spec in writing. A quote should list the number of treads, any landings, the pad density and whether the install is waterfall. If it just says stairs, ask for more.
Plan the day. A straight flight takes a few hours, and Everett is about 15 minutes from our Lynnwood showroom, so it is done before the dog needs its afternoon walk.

faq.q: Is carpet or hardwood safer for dogs on stairs?
faq.a: Carpet, by a wide margin. Hardwood treads are slick for claws, and a dog that slips once starts hesitating or jumping the last three steps, which is how joint injuries happen. Dense textured cut pile gives paws something to grip. If you love wood stairs, a bound runner is the compromise.

faq.q: Is berber carpet okay on stairs with dogs?
faq.a: We advise against it. Berber and other loops snag on claws, and one pulled loop on a nosing turns into a run across the whole tread. Small, calm dogs may never cause a problem, but with a large or excitable dog, textured cut pile is the safer bet.

faq.q: What pile height is best for dog stairs?
faq.a: Low to medium, roughly half an inch or less, with high density. Deep pile feels luxurious but compresses under a dog's landing weight, rounds off the tread edge and traps hair. Low, dense pile keeps the nosing crisp so the dog feels where the step ends.

faq.q: How do I clean dog hair off carpeted stairs?
faq.a: Use a handheld vacuum or a stair tool weekly, working the corner where tread meets riser. A rubber squeegee or damp rubber glove pulls embedded hair out of low pile fast. Have the stairs extracted with the rest of the house every 12 to 18 months.

faq.q: Will a stain warranty cover dog urine on stairs?
faq.a: Read carefully. Most fiber warranties exclude pet urine unless a specific pet warranty is named, and none cover the pad. Solution-dyed nylon and triexta are your real protection, because they let you clean aggressively without bleaching out the color.
